mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has risen monotonically from +9.7% to +16.9% over four weeks, indicating sustained home-based activity. This signals weakening demand for out-of-home retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL declines by more than 5 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has collapsed from -3.4% to -40.3% over three weeks, signaling mass workplace closure or remote work adoption. Commuting-dependent retail footfall (lunch, transit-adjacent shopping) will remain suppressed, keeping RETAIL_REC negative for the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -35% in any week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers to above -20% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -15%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has declined sharply from -10.0% to -26.7%, indicating reduced public transport use. This suppresses incidental retail visits by commuters and reduces foot traffic to retail clusters near transit hubs, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to above -15% and RETAIL_REC does not remain below -20% in the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains elevated (35.6% to 41.1%) while RETAIL_REC is deeply negative (-24.9% to -26.0%), indicating consumers are prioritizing essential shopping over discretionary retail. This bifurcation persists because essential-goods demand is inelastic, suppressing the recovery of non-essential retail over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +30% while RETAIL_REC remains below -20%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -15% while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +30%, indicating substitution reversal.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has remained consistently negative (-19.3% to -21.1%) across four weeks, indicating outdoor recreation is suppressed. This suggests either weather constraints or mobility restrictions that also suppress retail-and-recreation visits, maintaining downward pressure on RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained between -19.3% and -21.1% across all four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -10% and RETAIL_REC does not follow within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The joint collapse of WORKPLACES (-40.3%), TRANSIT (-26.7%), and PARKS (-21.1%) in the most recent week signals a coordinated policy tightening (lockdown or capacity restrictions). Under such regimes, retail closures or capacity caps directly constrain RETAIL_REC, which will remain suppressed for the next four weeks regardless of consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES < -35% AND TRANSIT < -25% AND PARKS < -20% in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:All three series hit extreme lows in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -15% within two weeks despite all three proxies remaining below their trigger thresholds.

If this reflects seasonal behavior (e.g., winter lockdown, holiday isolation), the trend will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks as consumers substitute home delivery and online shopping for in-person retail.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at +16.9% (t-0w), highest in the series
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines below +10% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -15% while RESIDENTIAL remains above +15%.

If this volatility reflects panic-buying cycles ending, consumers may reallocate spending back to discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week after reaching +50%
